articleTitle: High Time Resolution, Low-Noise, Power-Efficient, Charge-Sensitive Amplifier in 40 nm Technology
abstract: Particle detection circuits are used for a wide range of applications from experimental physics to material testing and medical imaging. In the state-of-the-art systems, the trend is to design low-noise and low-power readout front-end electronics with a low detection error rate and small silicon area occupation. This paper presents the design of a high time resolution, low-noise, and power-efficient charge sensitive amplifier (CSA) in 40 nm CMOS technology. For every charge pulse of the detector, the CSA generates voltage signals with a peak amplitude of 30.6 mV, a rise time of 2.35 ns, and an equivalent noise charge (ENC) of 44e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> with 0.14 mW power consumption.

articleTitle: Case Study of Electromagnetic Interference in Surgery Environment
abstract: In this paper, a case of electromagnetic interference (EMI) in medical display systems is reported. It concerns the nearby use of an electrosurgical knife disturbing video-monitors, interconnected by Ready-Made Connecting Devices (RMCD), in a surgery room. Based on full wave simulations, three parameters of these RMCD in a medical display installation, including the total length, location of connecting and the number of GND reference - wires, are identified. The simulation results demonstrate that these parameters can not only lead to EMI but are also influencing the characteristics of such EMI.

articleTitle: Reliability of low-power stepper motor drivers
abstract: Positional motion drives are widely used in various mechanical systems and machineries. These systems can be divided such as servomotor drives and stepper motor drives. This motion drives consist of the following system - “control electronic unit” and “positional motor”. Considering stepper motors drives on the point of view of reliability shows that the stepper motor has high reliability and the significant factor for the reliability of the stepper drives are their control units - so called stepper motor drivers. In this paper are considered low-power stepper motors drivers and their reliability.

articleTitle: Energy Performance Analysis of LoRaWAN End Device with Autonomous Power Supply
abstract: In recent years, LoRaWAN (LongRange Wide area Network) has attracted the attention of the community dealing with sensor networks and communications and their application in the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial IoT. It is a key technology in building a Low-Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) because it provides reliable low-power data transmission. An essential point and challenge in the application of this technology is ensuring maximum autonomy of LoRaWAN end devices by achieving the lowest possible energy consumption in sleep and active mode and the search for efficient power supply solutions. In this paper, a solution for autonomous powering of a LoRaWAN end device with a photovoltaic panel and optimization of energy consumption in different operating modes is proposed and investigated. A system has been developed for monitoring, analysis and visualization of end device consumption.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Classification via Machine Learning Model Inference on Homomorphic Encrypted Medical Data
abstract: This paper studies the use of homomorphic encryption to preserve privacy when using machine learning classifiers. The paper compares different parameters and explores drawbacks in terms of accuracy, speed, and packet size when using encrypted data versus unencrypted data by using a client-server use case. These comparisons were performed during multiple tests on different datasets with different sizes and complexity. These tests show it is possible to do machine learning with homomorphic encrypted data without losing accuracy. However, the increased processing time, data size and communication time have to be considered.

articleTitle: Application of Logistic Regression Technique for Predicting Student Dropout
abstract: Student dropout in higher education is a complex issue and as a process it includes many factors which may affect each other. This paper explores the use and application of a probabilistic supervised machine learning technique for predicting university student dropout to obtain insights on the students at risk and prevent them from dropping out the studies. Data from a public university in the Republic of Kosovo were obtained and examined. The dataset comprises instances of students' dropouts for the past six academic years along with their demographics, grades, enrollment details etc. Logistic Regression, as one of the most widely used Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence algorithms, was used to build the model and produce the predictions. First, a statistical analysis was conducted and after the data preprocessing, logistic regression classifier was implemented. The results show that a high prediction accuracy was reached, with a percentage of 90%, and a F1 score of 0.85, indicating that the model is performing great and the predictions results are reliable.

articleTitle: Basic Dependencies of a Phase-Shift Controlled LLC DC-DC Converter at Continuous Current Mode
abstract: In this paper the basic dependencies describing the electromagnetic processes in phase-shift controlled LLC DC-DC Converter operating in Continuous Current Mode are discussed. As a result, normalized expressions for calculation of the most important circuit quantities are obtained. The boundary conditions for the transition between the possible converter operating modes under output voltage regulation are determined. The obtained analytical results are confirmed by simulation studies.

articleTitle: Virtual Instrument for Capacitance Measurement of Supercapacitor Cells as part of an Energy Storage System
abstract: This article presents an idea for developing virtual instrument based on LabVIEW and used for dynamic measurement of the capacitance of supercapacitors cells. The cells are part of an energy storage system, where they are connected in series in order to form a battery pack with the desired voltage level. The capacitance measurement is achievable during both charge and discharge stages directly when the battery is in use. An experimental set up with four series connected cells has been developed for testing and verifying the reliability of the virtual instrument.

articleTitle: Determining the Focal Length of a Video Camera Using a Calibration Pattern
abstract: The article discusses a method for determining the focal length of a video camera lens using a calibration pattern in the form of a checkerboard. Methods for determining the focal length of the lens are considered. An analysis of methods for measuring the focal length of a lens (magnification method, Fabry-Yudin method, goniometric method) showed that additional optical systems must be used in these methods. A method for determining the focal length of a video camera lens is proposed. It is shown that the results obtained by the proposed method are close to the focal lengths of the camera lenses.

articleTitle: Mobile Low-cost Air Pollution Data Logger
abstract: Air quality is one of the most important factors for human life. It is vital to monitor indoor and outdoor air parameters and to do appropriate measures. In the recent years the technology advances increasingly and that makes possible to produce many types of low-cost sensors and microcontrollers that have low power consumption. In this article the developed low-cost mobile system for air quality monitoring is presented. The results from initial measurements in eight points in the Plovdiv city center are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Development of a Network Camera with a Built-in Mask and QR Code Recognition Function
abstract: Therefore, in different environments and places, we can use the network camera of the video surveillance system to detect whether people are wearing masks, and scan the OR code to obtain their information. Based on the collection and analysis of scene data by network cameras, this paper adopts a deep learning method, that is, the detection of mask wearing conditions can be realized through training on the face data of labeled masks, and this technology is combined with QR code recognition technology. It is also built into the network camera. In the current context, the research of this technology has very important value and significance for epidemic control during this period. Due to the outbreak of covid 19 in 2019, in order to prevent the epidemic, this article designed a network camera with a built in mask and QR code recognition function for video surveillance and access control system development.

articleTitle: Study of Limiting Factors in the Selection of a Learning Sample of Images for Automatic Tracking of Changes in Weather Conditions
abstract: In our previous work on using images from stationary outdoor cameras for tracking the loss of visibility, we analysed a series of videos taken from different localizations. The results showed the need of big data processing, and also the presence of situations that would lead to mis-identification of loss of visibility without its availability. The material shows the cases of such situations and the need of consideration of the camera localization, its orientation and the current position of the sun.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning for Teaching the Topic “Design of Differentiators and Integrators in MATLAB” in Digital Signal Processing Course
abstract: The paper presents the use of the collaborative learning approach when teaching the topic “Design of Differentiators and Integrators in MATLAB” in the Course “Digital Signal Processing” during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some issues about digital differentiators and integrators are described in the paper as well as the problems solved by students during the workshops and students' feedback about their satisfaction with this approach.

articleTitle: LabVIEW ECG and Noise Simulator for Advanced Synthesis of Machine Learning Databases
abstract: This study aims to develop an advanced simulator of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and overlaid noises (electromyogram, power-line interference, baseline wander, white noise), which benefits the extended functionality of the LabVIEW Biomedical Toolkit. Interactive interface handles the visualization of time and spectral behavior of ECG, noise and mixed ECG+noise signals from Physionet databanks or artificial signal generators with advanced morphological and frequency controls. Noise-free and noisy ECG databases with fixed or randomized behavior can be thereby created for the purpose of data augmentation in machine learning arrhythmia detection strategies, or for standard performance testing of diagnostic electrocardiographs.

articleTitle: Criminal Liability Associated with Artificial Intelligence Entities under the Bulgarian Criminal Law
abstract: The present article is dedicated to the problem of ascribing criminal liability related to development, deployment and use of artificial intelligence (AI) entities. The well-known three legal models proposed by G. Hallevy are discussed. A comparative analysis between the relevant Bulgarian Criminal law concepts and the three models is offered in order to find out whether they are applicable in Bulgaria. Possible solutions under the Bulgarian Criminal law are discussed. In the conclusion the results of the analysis are summarized.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Boost DC-DC Converters with Application in Power Electronics Education
abstract: The paper presents a comparative analysis of DC-DC converters that can be successfully utilized in the education of power electronic converters. A comparative analysis is made against four boost converter topologies, which essentially demonstrates the advantages and disadvantages of the practical realization of one and the same DC/DC converter. These are the synchronous and non-synchronous converter and the internal and external switch converters. The hardware realization of the compared evaluation boards is suitable for training of both students and professionals in the field, because they are intended to be simple but in the same time with all the standard features and maximum performance.

articleTitle: A Vital Parameters Monitoring System Using Capacitive Electrodes
abstract: The vital signs monitoring systems are gaining more and more importance in the world of communications and intelligent devices. There are different types of devices monitoring different vital parameters. In this work a device monitoring the human breathing while laid on the bed over a sheet with a matrix of capacitive electrodes is developed. The capacitance of the body to the electrodes can be used to tell the laying pose and the breathing of the person. The system can be also used for quality of sleep measurements. Following the capacitance of the body to the matrix of electrodes can give a lot of information about the person lying on the bed.

articleTitle: Embedded Power Management System for Mobile Service Robots
abstract: The autonomous operation of mobile service robots is provided by a portable electric energy source, usually a rechargeable battery pack. This article presents complete power management solutions for small service robots based on a lithium-ion battery pack. It consists of two main parts: a battery management system (BMS) and an intelligent charging module with USB-C power delivery input. This architecture allows the safe and reliable operation of the battery under various working conditions. All battery data is available to the main computer via the System Management Bus (SMBus) interface.

articleTitle: Piezo Effect of Collagen Layer with Rochelle Salt Nanocrystals
abstract: A piezo layer from Collagen was deposited by electrophoresis for bio-electronics needs. Natural piezo materials are characterized with low piezo module. The value of the piezo module is increased by electrophoretic deposition (EPD) of Rochelle Salt/Collagen. The resulting layer consists of a Rochelle Salt nanocrystalline sublayer and inhomogeneously distributed Collagen aggregates on it. This layer has a high piezo response comparable to inorganic piezo materials.

articleTitle: Application of System Diversity for IncreasingSecurity and Reliability of Distributed Systems
abstract: This article quantifies the application of system diversity to increase the reliability and security of communications in geographically distributed computer systems. Based on the multidimensional stress strength analysis and the classical theory, new models have been proposed, and new analytical dependencies have been derived, which can be used to quantify the increase in reliability and security of distributed systems.

articleTitle: Modern Teaching Methods Used for Representing the Topic “Implementations of Carry-Skip Adders”
abstract: The paper describes the application of modern teaching methods for representing the topic “Implementations of Carry-Skip Adders” based on various computer tools, such as MS Excel, Logisim, and ISE Project Navigator, intended for the undergraduate students from the specialty “Computer Systems and Technologies” studying the course “Digital Electronics” at the University of Ruse “Angel Kanchev”.

articleTitle: Output Characteristics for Continuous Current Mode of a Phase-Shift Controlled LLC DC-DC Converter
abstract: The following paper presents a study of a phase-shift controlled LLC DC-DC converter. It is assumed that the resonant frequency of the tank circuit series branch is lower than the operating frequency. The study based on the output characteristics of the converter is mainly related to the continuous current mode at the rectifier input.

articleTitle: Bluetooth Low Energy Reliability and Throughput under Wi-Fi Interference
abstract: In this paper, the performance of Bluetooth Low Energy is studied under different Wi-Fi interference. Two aspects of BLE performance are investigated, namely reliability and throughput. According to the practical experiment results, both the reliability as well as the throughput are highly impacted by Wi-Fi interference. Besides, a new discovery is that the impacts of interference on the two performance aspects are not proportional to one another. This research can be utilized by other studies as a proof or cornerstone.

articleTitle: Technology for Multiplication and Analysis of Results Using Classes of Digital Twins in the Process of Designing Business Process Management Systems
abstract: This article analyzes the prerequisites for more rational management of the product life cycle and more correct and accurate collection, analysis and risk-free dissemination of data when designing a PLM system based on Strategy, Process, Product Architecture and IT Architecture. In order to shorten the design and product engineering cycles, the implementation of PLM-S through a set of virtual “Digital Twins” and “Cognitive Digital Twin” models, which are connected to their physical “twins” via IoT and managed in PLM systems, is considered. The threats and opportunities in the management of the real-time data flow, the implementation and full use of PLM systems are systematized.

articleTitle: Study of Lead-Free Perovskite Solar Cells at Elevated Temperatures and UV Irradiation
abstract: In the present work, the change of the electrical performance is investigated for two lead-free perovskite materials with novel iodide-based and bromide-based compositions under different exploitation conditions, such as light-induced stress, elevated temperatures and ultraviolet light exposure. The charge transport properties are studied in more detail by spectroscopic methods for the cell with the iodide layer due to its greater stability, aiming to understand the degradation mechanism. The results show that this perovskite exhibited excellent stability at UV exposure and acceptable stability at continuous illumination at 600 nm. The device is stable up to 55 °C, when the photovoltage drops. Beyond this threshold temperature, a phase change transition occurs related to traps formation and charge carriers escaping, which affects the photovoltage and it slightly increases.

articleTitle: Application of Accelerometer for Vehicle Parameterization
abstract: Accelerometer and magnetic sensor data fusion shows promising results for vehicle classification applications in a smart city. In this paper, the following algorithms for accelerometer data usage are proposed: extraction of axle times and locations, speed calculation and magnetic signature correction. Examples are shown to suggest the usage of the algorithms: classification to 4 vehicle types including trailer detection, speed estimation method, which is more accurate than a traditional one and correction of magnetic signatures for various purposes.

articleTitle: Inventory Approach for Managing Income-Expenditure Deficit
abstract: A quantitative solution for managing the deficit between incomes and expenditure of an enterprise is derived. The management in content is presented as planning a safe amount of financial resources for covering the potential deficit, which arises on monthly bases as a difference between due disbursements and available incomes. The quantitative model is based on the usage of inventory theory for planning safety stock for a given level of service. The quantitative approach is applied to the real data, taken from the balance sheet of husbandry from the region of Stara Zagora.

articleTitle: Algorithm for traffic management with priority for emergency vehicles
abstract: One of the major problems in modern cities is the heavy street traffic which can be a significant problem even for the emergency vehicles like ambulances and fire brigades. The present paper provides a brief description of the existing technology means for traffic management. By means of contemporary technologies, an appropriate solution for providing a priority passing of the special vehicles can be created. The paper aims to offer an algorithm for the fast movement of emergency vehicles in conditions of heavy road traffic. The presented smart traffic management system implements several nowadays technologies such as a cloud-based control center, image processing, and GPS tracking and navigation. The conceptions of data traffic management and cloud-based control center are explained, and the advantages of replacing the RFID tags with smart technologies are presented.

articleTitle: Embedded System for Detecting Underwater Ultrasound
abstract: The current paper focuses on the implementation details of a device that detects ultrasound at a distance of 1 m in sea water. This detector could be used to test the operation of ultrasonic emitting devices, called pingers, which deter cetacean mammals from entering fish nets of fishing boats at sea. The device is battery-powered and a low-energy Bluetooth connection is available for turning it on and off.

articleTitle: Switch Time Activation Function and Stopit Regression - Some Examples
abstract: In neural networks, single neuron can be considered as a generalization of a regression model and the activation function is the function which is applied to the output of a neuron to obtain some specific, generally non-linear type of transformation of the input signals. Here we consider Switch Time activation function and stopit regression based on using Switch Time distribution.

articleTitle: Safety Case Conversion from Goal Structuring Notation to Structured Assurance Case Metamodel
abstract: Assurance cases are a valuable tool in communicating arguments for the justification of system properties. Graphical notations provide a clear way to presents these arguments. However, many commercial tools fail to implement recent standards and provide no support to the transition between notations. This paper presents an assurance case tool fit to the most recent guidelines, providing support for multiple notations with the abiliy to convert a safety case to a different notation.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Study of Infrared Detectors with Lead-Free Perovskite Films at Different Electrode Designs
abstract: This study presents results on the implementation of lead-free perovskite films and quantum dots with a silicon substrate as a photodetector for the near infrared range of the electromagnetic spectrum. Two different electrode designs with strip and comb patterns are realized to investigate and compare the basic parameters of the devices at different wavelengths, optical power intensities, and illumination angles. The most favorable sensitivity and linearity are measured for the device with the strip patterned electrodes at a wavelength of 860 nm. For this case, a responsivity of 7.24 mA/W, detectivity of 181x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> Jones, external quantum efficiency of 94 %, and response time of 1.3 μs are obtained.

articleTitle: Maximum power point tracking in photovoltaic system by step-down converter
abstract: The operation of step down DC-DC converter, fed by photovoltaic panel is considered. Expressions have been obtained to determine operating and energy characteristics during steady-state modes at maximum input power. Several results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Modeling of Microfluidic Cell with Electrodes for Impedance Measurements
abstract: In this work is presented computational fluid dynamics modeling of a microfluidic cell with electrodes for impedance measurements. Internal channels cross-section architecture is considered according to fluid dynamic pressure drop and capillary resistance. Results for fluid flow dynamics in the microfluidic cell are acquired and presented. Considerations on electrodes design and contact surface are made according to equivalent circuit model of the mixing chamber of the fluidic cell. Numerical results about expected impedance of NaCl solution are obtained and presented.

articleTitle: Determining the Suitability of Measurement Circuits for Piezoelectric Vibrational Harvesters
abstract: The precise determination of an acquired energy from energy harvester type devices is one of the most important tasks in their designing process as the main difficulty is the relatively miniscule energy amount that should be precisely evaluated for better estimation of their power yield. Therefore the measurement circuit is one of the more important things in determining the energy output.

articleTitle: Sensing Pad for Pressure Distribution Mapping
abstract: Here is presented an interactive sensing pad for pressure distribution mapping in wide surface area. The main task of the work is to prototype a concept of a sensing pad for continuous pressure distribution detection over a wide surface. Further, the sensing pad could be integrated in an IoT communication system. The main concept of the work is pressure sensing over two applicable technologies and an estimation in order to find the optimal solution based on design efficiency, complexity, cost, and durability criteria. Also, the main limitations of the two discussed pressure sensing technologies are demonstrated. Realized at the current stage prototypes of sensing pad design elements are shown.

articleTitle: Applying Aniline for P-doping of PEDOT:PSS Films to Improve Their Conductivity and Efficiency of Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Poly(3,4- ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT: PSS) is responsible for hole extraction efficiency and hole transport in the perovskite solar cell structure. The inclusion of PSS reduces the conductivity of the PEDOT films, which inhibits hole transport and results in a low photo current of the perovskite solar cell. In this work, an aniline solution was used as an additive in the PEDOT: PSS thin film to increase electrical conductivity. Two different methods were used to incorporate the additive: surface and volume treatment. The results show that the surface treatment with aniline solution can significantly increase the conductivity of PEDOT: PSS film. Moreover, the photoconversion efficiency of the perovskite solar cell with such a PEDOT: PSS layer is increased 1.5 times compared to the untreated one.

articleTitle: Electroless and Electrochemical Copper Deposition to Form a Conductive Layer on Anodized Aluminum Substrate
abstract: In the present work, the possibility of electroless deposition of copper layers on nanoporous anodic alumina oxide on an aluminum base has been studied. For this purpose, a weakly acidic copper electrolyte was used for electroless deposition at pH values from 4.1 to 6.1. The copper layers are thickened by electrochemical deposition of copper. The thickness, uniformity along the length of the samples and the sheet resistance on the obtained layers were measured.

articleTitle: Research of low-power stepper motor drivers
abstract: During the last decade stepper motor driver manufacturers perform a wide range of activities to increase functional and parameters. The manufacturers direct their efforts to create specialized integrated circuits with a very high degree of functionality. The guidelines in the development of stepper motor drivers are related to: high degree of integration of transistors and logic function blocks in the integrated circuits; microstep modes, low resistance power MOSFET transistors and additional function such as reducing of idle current, specialized control interface (UART, SPI).

articleTitle: FPGA Based Architecture for Test and Release of Custom Datapath in Pure RTL Designs
abstract: In pure RTL based design, the major difficulty is to prepare and provide a verification procedure on soft IDE in case of big quantities of test data. If the desire datapath is still unverified - this task will take many working time of high qualified RTL designers. In this paper an architecture method of processing and FPGA based board for test and release is described. It can decrease of working time of RTL designers in test and verification stages and time-to-market in release stage.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Digital and Analog Compensation for VRM
abstract: Fulfilling the tight requirements of automotive grade switched mode power supplies depends on the optimal design of its compensation network. Choosing and implementing the right type of compensation can make or break the dynamic performance of the converter. For this reason, this paper examines both digital and analog compensators and their behavior.

articleTitle: Traffic control optimization in the priority direction
abstract: The paper works out a mathematical model for urban traffic control on a network of five crossroads. The goal of the research is simultaneous optimization of green light and cycle duration giving priority to one direction. The bi-level hierarchical optimization is the applied formalization methodology. The optimization problems of both hierarchical levels are derived. The bi-level optimal results are compared with those from classical one-level optimization problem. The influence of the model's parameters is analyzed.

articleTitle: Model for Determination of Relative Humidity at Every Point in Cross-Section in Residential Premises
abstract: The paper presents a mathematical model developed in MATLAB programming environment, which is used to obtain information about the value of relative humidity at a selected point in a cross-section, formed by six points in living space. The results show that the proposed model describes the measured relative humidity in height over time. During daylight hours, the relative humidity is lower in the higher parts of the room compared to the lower parts. In the dark part of the day the results show that the trend of the change of relative humidity, relative to the height of the room, is below 1% and favors the higher parts of the room. By means of the developed model, rooms with larger geometry and larger differences in measured relative humidity between floor and ceiling can be evaluated by the similarity method.

articleTitle: Over-discharge Phenomenon Caused by Corona Discharge in Lithium-ion Batteries (LiB) and its Effect on Copper Dissolution from the Negative Current Collector
abstract: Assuming that a lithium-ion battery (LiB) is left in the vicinity of a high-voltage device, we generated corona discharge in the prototype LiB and verified that over-discharge occurs. During an over-discharge test using a constant current with a similar average current (18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A})$</tex>, the voltage did not maintain a constant value near 0 V, and a drop in voltage below -0.9 V was observed. After the test, the prototype cell was disassembled and the separator and electrodes were observed. It was found that copper dissolution from the negative current collector was hardly observed in the case of over-discharge by corona discharge However, in the case of over-discharge with constant current, copper dissolution was significant. This difference is suggested to be caused by the fact that the corona discharge current is in the form of pulses. And as a result of an over-discharge test using a pulse current of 100 kHz duty 10%, a phenomenon was observed in which the voltage remained constant around 0 V as in the case of corona discharge. Furthermore, the current distribution inside the negative porous electrode during the application of pulsed current was analyzed using a transmission line model. The current distribution in the electrodes is different for pulsed currents from constant currents. It was found that current inversion occurs through the electric double layer and the current distribution through the charge transfer resistance becomes smaller during the quiescent period of the current.

articleTitle: The eXtended Reality Technology in Power System Trainings
abstract: New technologies and digital trainings can support engineers and technicians to operate and maintain wind park in power system more efficiently. The purpose of the paper is focused on the demand of employer's training with new immersive and advanced technologies that offer better training, and results in the enhancement of employers' skills and their performance. A method for creating trainings that are interactive, scalable, and adaptable have been proposed by using the eXtended reality technology.

articleTitle: Autonomous Smart Wireless LoRaWAN Vehicle Parking Sensor
abstract: This paper presents the use of a battery powered LoRaWAN ultrasonic sensor node for the realization of autonomous smart LoRaWAN vehicle parking sensor. In particular, the paper presents the possibility of using LoRaWAN waterproof ultrasonic sensor node powered by solar harvester systems to manage the parking area. The hardware design and software implementation of the sensor node are presented. The designed and implemented sensor node was actually tested under external atmospheric conditions to guarantee its autonomous operation.

articleTitle: Creating an basic IoT 3D farming model
abstract: In this paper are described creating an basic IoT 3D farming model. The idea is to to automate lettuce cultivation, process management and data tracking. For this purpose, technologies such as Raspberry Pi, air humidity sensors, soil moisture level, culture illumination, temperature and air humidity measurement, CO2 amount measurement, atmospheric pressure measurement and air flow control, heat are used and illumination.

articleTitle: Software and Hardware Infrastructure for Research and Development of Intelligent Control for Robotic Manipulators
abstract: This research proposes a hardware and software infrastructure for development of control algorithms for robotic manipulators. The algorithms can be developed entirely in a simulation environment and independently of the physical robot, which speeds up their development. The proposed methodology requires the development of additional software modules to be used for input-output operations. They allow the control algorithm to be independent from the environment. The conducted experiments proved that the infrastructure is suitable for research and development of control algorithms.

articleTitle: Design and Energy Production Research of a 28,8 kW PhotoVoltaic System
abstract: The article presents the design, simulation, construction and research of a 28,8 kW photovoltaic system in the mountainous region of Smolyan, Bulgaria by a team of professors and students at the University of Plovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski”. Students acquire permanent knowledge and develop skills for working with software for the design and optimization of photovoltaic systems, as well as skills for designing systems for generating energy from renewable energy sources. The parameters of the Photoelectric Plant were studied. An analysis of the simulation data from the design was performed with the actual measured and obtained data for electricity production for a period of one year.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Life Span of PV Inverter
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the life span of the photovoltaic inverter and its components. The basic methodology for estimation of the transistors and capacitors in the inverter are presented. The proposed solutions are useful for definition of the time for exploitation and how the energy efficiency of the photovoltaic system could be improved by rehabilitating the inverter and its components.

articleTitle: Utilization of Pure Glass Composite Interference Wedged Structures as Highly Efficient Light Beam Splitters
abstract: We present a developed approach for analysis and optimization of new, pure glass light beam splitters as instrumentation, especially for high intensity laser beam splitting. The method is based on our previously introduced Composed Interference Wedged Structures. The linear division from 100% to 10% is performed via sliding a plate splitter in a range of 50 mm. Among the advantages of the method are no change of direction of the formed beams, no polarization requirements, low losses, maintenance.

articleTitle: A Cycle-accurate Template Microprocessor Model of a Von Neumann Architecture Based on SystemC
abstract: The paper presents different aspects of the creation of a cycle-accurate, pipeline-accurate, single-issue, von Neumann microprocessor model that can be used as a template to model any existing microarchitecture. The goal of this development is simplicity and modularity so that any embedded developer could create a model out of the instruction timings given in the datasheet. The model is created as a separate entity to allow for code reuse and support for many families and sub-families of microcontrollers.

articleTitle: A Review of Supercapacitors State of Health Estimation Methods
abstract: Supercapacitors are entering massively as an important supporting technology for energy storage in various fields of application such as electric vehicles, power grid, renewable energy, and home applications. The reliable operation of these systems requires accurate prediction of the state of health (SOH) of the supercapacitors. This necessitates the development and application of various methods to estimate the lifetime of the supercapacitor during system design and optimization. In this paper, a summary of the main methods for evaluating the SOH of supercapacitors is made, as well as future research directions are outlined.

articleTitle: Stabilizing the Strength of Solders in LGA Electronic Assembly by Different Design of Pads and Using of Statistical Evaluation Methods
abstract: The article describes the study of the strength of solders in LGA (Land grid array) assembly. The influence of the design of the pads of the boards on the strength of the solders is considered. The breaking force measurement was performed with a specialized intelligent measurement system. Statistical methods were used to analyze the breaking force of solders. Best design conclusions regarding solder strength are drawn and future research to obtain stable and strong solders is suggested.

articleTitle: Implementation of harness testing device using microcontroller
abstract: The paper describes the developed microcontroller device for testing and controlling the production of cable harnesses in the automotive industry. Based on the results of the testing, a decision is made as to how and whether the work process can continue through logical management of the implemented mechanisms in the system. The device has been implemented in production at the plant of the Hronovski company in the town of Smolyan. The cable harnesses are used in the production of automotive lighting systems, such as taillights, front lights, daytime running lights and auxiliary lights. The tester is suitable for use in engineering education and training of industry professionals. It is used to teach microcontrollers, programming, and testing and diagnostics in the mass production at Plovdiv University “Paisii Hilendarski” - Faculty of Physics and Technology. Modern production requires high expert potential from those working in it, direct interaction between universities and industry, and this is done with the use of modern effective environments, methods and tools.

articleTitle: Personal Identification Based Automatic Face Annotation in Multi-View Systems
abstract: We propose a method for automatic face annotation in a closed multi-view environment. In such an environment faces are automatically detected and images are collected from several sources. Then, for the purpose of real-time labelling, a model is incrementally trained with every new person who enters the environment. The incremental learning model is validated on the Pandora dataset, which is split into different classes for each incremental step. Active learning is used to determine the type of images needed for training based on a predefined budget.

articleTitle: SPICE Modeling of Off-line Switchers from the TinySwitch Family
abstract: This paper is devoted to the modeling of the TinySwitch family of efficient power conversion ICs. A generalized block diagram of the structure of the individual generations of the family is presented, which is used as a basis for synthesizing a suitable SPICE subcircuit applicable for modeling the individual representatives of the family. Verification of the presented model with comparison of the simulated performance of a specific integrated circuit with a real experiment is performed.

articleTitle: 2D PtTe2 Layers Synthesized by Thermally Assisted Conversion Method
abstract: Scalable production and controlled doping of large-area two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide films are fundamental steps toward their applications in electronic and opto-electronic devices. Although a variety of methods for preparation of wafer-scale transition-metal dichalcogenide films have been developed, they still need further elaboration to satisfy the high quality requirements for application-grade materials. Here we report the synthesis of 2D PtTe2 by direct tellurization of pre-deposited thin Pt film of various thickness on soda lime glass substrates.

articleTitle: Open-loop Software Automatic Gain Control: Common-mode Power-line Interference Stabilization During ECG Recording
abstract: Automatic gain control (AGC) units are widespread in modern telecommunication systems. The main function of AGC is to stabilize the amplitude of the processed signal. AGC generates a constant amplitude output signal when the input signal level changes. This article describes an all-digital architecture for automatic open-loop gain control designed to generate constant amplitude of the power-line interference extracted from the common-mode signal during ECG biopotential recording. The presented open-loop AGC has a very simple architecture and can be applied to other applications where AGC functionality is needed.

articleTitle: An Adjustable Amplifier for Capacitive ECG Registration
abstract: The recording of the electrical activity of the heart using capacitive electrodes has been the subject of permanent interest by researchers because of the undisputable advantage in terms of convenience for the patient compared to the widely used techniques using conventional electrodes. This paper presents a variant of an analog input amplifier in which, unlike existing similar implementations, it is possible to change the amplification depending on the electrode capacitance, as well as to realize continuous automatic suppression of the DC offset at the input of the amplifier. The results of simulation studies performed in an LTspice are presented, as well as signals recorded by a volunteer. The ability to automatically adjust the DC offset at the amplifier input allows the use of a low supply voltage, which is important for applications in portable stand-alone devices.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Compensation of Differential Nonlinearity in Digital-to-Analog Converters
abstract: The differential nonlinearity is one of the most common error sources in the Digital-to-Analog Converters. Higher values of differential nonlinearity can lead to non-monotonic transfer function of the converter. If the differential nonlinearity is with negative sign it can be corrected by adjustment of the digital code. The positive differential nonlinearities cannot be corrected. A methodology for measurement, calculation and code adjustment is proposed and tested in this paper.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication and Measurements of Microstrip Patch Antenna at 2.66 GHz
abstract: This article discusses the considerations for designing a rectangular microband antenna to operate at a resonant frequency of 2.66 GHz. The design includes analytical calculation of the geometry of the antenna, simulation of the design using specialized software for preliminary evaluation of the parameters and verification of the results through experimental measurements of a prototype. Experimental measurements of the prototype made with a filter and without it show that the prepared antenna is characterized by very good characteristics for the selected resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Embedded System for Radiation Pattern Measurements of Antennas
abstract: The rapid development of wireless systems requires the use of suitable antennas for high-frequency applications. This leads to continuous improvement of techniques and systems for measuring the basic parameters of these antennas. In this article, we present our embedded system for radiation pattern measurements of antennas. It consists of hardware and software and is designed to work in laboratory conditions. It can be used to measure the characteristics of antennas with different weights and sizes operating in different frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Development of GSM Modem for Transfer of ECG Signals in Remote Patient Monitoring
abstract: The remote patient monitoring is more important in these days. With the development of the modern technologies the distant ECG signal monitoring is becoming more common although if the patients are elderly people they will have trouble using modern communication technologies. Also many places have no good network coverage. For these situations an ECG module communicating with audio signals is implemented using the standard telephone or GSM line for transmission of the data. For this purpose, a GSM modem is developed and tested for receiving the ECG audio data.

articleTitle: Method to Support Lithium-Ion Batteries' Operation at Low Temperatures
abstract: A method for supporting the operation of 18650 lithium - ion batteries at low temperatures is presented. The developed method is applicable to other types of lithium-ion batteries, providing the same power for electric heating of all batteries in a battery pack. The results showed that the developed heating method ensures the lithium-ion batteries to reach in just a few minutes the recommended temperature range for their safe operation, even at very low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{(below~ \text{-}20^{\circ}C)}$</tex> ambient temperatures.

articleTitle: Design of Fractional Filters for Power-line Interference Suppression in ECG Signals
abstract: The sampling interval is the unit step in which a discrete biosignal can be easily shifted during the digital filtering process. It allows the design of linear-phase filters with constant group delay characteristics. In many cases, the sampling interval is insufficiently short to ensure the required frequency response of the filter. This paper presents a novel approach for design of fractional filters, which is applied to several common types of comb filters. The effectiveness of the approach is illustrated by filtering of the power-line interference in real ECG signals. The presented fractional filters have a simple design, which is suitable to different biosignal acquisition applications where filtering of various noises is strongly mandatory.

articleTitle: Application of B-Scan for identification of delamination in Integrated Circuits
abstract: In this paper the application of B-Scan mode of surface acoustic microscopy for detection of delamination is investigated. Delamination is a common defect found in integrated circuits. It consists of presence of air cavities between layers in encapsulated integrated circuits. B-Scan is a technique for vertical inspection of the layers composing the device under test. The use of B-Scan mode to unambiguous identify the presence or absence of delamination is examined in details. The results are verified by A-Scan and 180°-phase shift of the reflected signal.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Control of Relocatable Lighting System
abstract: With the improvement of technology and the concept of the Internet of Things, more and more attention is being performed to intelligent control systems. Many mathematical models and processing of big data sets are applied. In this paper, an approach for implement mobile lighting control system based on fuzzy logic is proposed. The system consists of illuminance sensors, low-cost wireless controllers and is built using the LabVIEW graphical programming environment.

articleTitle: A Review of State of Health Battery Diagnostics Methods: Current Status and Future Challenges
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used power sources for modern systems as renewable and sustainable energy storage devices. Problems with their safe operation caused by inaccurate assessment of their state of health SOH can lead to significant losses in terms of facilities, environment, and people. In this article, the three main methods for evaluating and predicting the SOH of lithium-ion batteries are systematized: model based, data driven and fusion technology methods. Future trends and perspectives in SOH estimation and prediction are discussed.

articleTitle: Modeling of Autonomous System with PV, Supercapacitor and Micro Hydro Power Plant
abstract: In this research a mathematical model of autonomous system with photovoltaic, supercapacitor and micro hydro power plant is presented. The model is realized in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Separate parts of the autonomous system are described and modeled using differential equations describing the principle of operation.

articleTitle: Development of Lines for Production of Electromechanical Products by Evaluating their Efficiency through Statistics and in the Conditions of Lean Manufacturing
abstract: The implementation of a project for the construction of a production line for the production of connectors was considered. Lean manufacturing was used to achieve optimal results regarding productivity and quality. The development of the line over time was reviewed in order to improve quality. By using statistics, an analysis was made to evaluate the line. In the conclusion, future developments and expected results are defined.

articleTitle: Investigation of Acoustic Barrier Sound Absorption with Different Radius
abstract: For the needs of acoustic noise attenuation, a 3D COMSOL model was developed. Some of its main parameters and characteristics are analysed and changed in order to obtain the best ratio between good attenuation and energy generation for the needs of energy harvesting at specific frequency range from 63 Hz to 2000 Hz. The developed models can be used for verification of noise-insulating barriers for acoustic applications.

articleTitle: Applying a Risk-based Approach for ensuring Network Connection Safety in a Maritime Environment
abstract: In this paper a risk-based approach is applied to a maritime use case in order to guarantee dependable operation of the involved network connection. The dynamic positioning control system is studied, specifically the network communication, and a case scenario is considered in which Electro-Magnetic Interference (EMI) induced failures remain undetected at the network level. Electromagnetic diversity is proposed as an electromagnetic resilience measure to deal with such EMI induced failures already at the network level.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Study on Electroless Cu-Ni-P Alloy
abstract: In the present work, the process of electroless deposition of Cu-Ni-P alloy layers using liner sweep voltammetry has been studied. The influence of temperature, pH of the electrolyte, as well as the concentration of nickel ions (in the form of NiSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) and the reducer (NaH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) on the cathodic reduction of copper and nickel and the anodic oxidation of the reducer was studied.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Contactless Power Transmission System Based on a Resonant Inverter
abstract: This paper's purpose is to demonstrate how to create a Qi 1.2 certified wireless charging system using a NXQ1TXH5 controller and driver IC. Because of the growing technological need of on-board charging and charging flexibility small size, high efficiency and high reliability are common standards for evaluating high-performance chargers. The design of the systems starts with researching and understanding how a full bridge resonant inverter functions. The main things that need to be understood for grasping this resonant inverter's method of operation are when and why the transistors in the bridge switch, the three main frequency modes of operating and the resonant circuit and its parameters e.g. Q-factor. Another part of this project is to understand and implementing the Qi 1.2 standard and all of its specifications and requirements. This standard covers two types of devices that are both required for the whole system to function: a receiver and a transmitter. The device presented in this paper is the ladder.

articleTitle: Building Independent Models of YouTube Content Networks as a Tool for Monitoring Health Misinformation
abstract: This article showcases a two-fold process for externally analyzing YouTube content recommendation paths. The first part is a simple tool for identifying video recommendations using Python and Google's API. The second part provides a sample workflow for mapping, analyzing, and visualizing the gathered data. The analysis is proposed as a tool for monitoring health misinformation online.

articleTitle: A Single Sensor Interior Lighting Control System for Constant Illuminance Level on Working Desks
abstract: In this paper an Internet of Things (IoT) based system for LED lighting is presented. A single sensor which measures the incoming daylight is used to control the illuminance in the entire room. A mathematical approximation is used to calculate the lighting levels in the different zones. The system is implemented in real conditions in order to keep a constant illuminance level in a production hall by replacing the existing LED lamps with intelligent ones. The improvement of the energy efficiency as a result of the system implementation is also discussed.

articleTitle: Research of the latest development trends for model-based design automotive mechatronics education
abstract: The paper presents a model-based automotive mechatronic device development methodology applied to student electronics training courses. The programming environment used is Matlab/Simulink. The methodology is tested using the project with low complexity in order to meet the short deadlines of the study process for the master's course on hybrid and electric vehicles at Technical University of Sofia.

articleTitle: Compact smart solid-state relay with WiFi connectivity
abstract: The smart homes has an important role of the carbon footprint reduction as the cities create an estimated 65% of global energy demand and cause 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. The conversion of the ordinary homes into the smart ones using the wireless technologies may reduce the energy use at the same time as supporting optimal comfort and convenience. The proposed compact smart solid-state relay with WiFi connectivity allows a remote control of the home environment to save energy and it also may be controlled via near-field communication such as RFID or NFC to automatically adjust the environment parameters.

articleTitle: Experimental Set-up for Sensors Selection for Early Fault Detection in Innovative Modular Li-Ion Battery Systems Related to HELIOS H2020 Project
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have already become a mainstream energy storage solution for many applications, especially for hybrid and electric vehicles (EV). Various malfunctions in the lithium-ion battery system (LIBS) can cause serious safety problems and significant performance determination. For the safe and efficient operation of LIBS, the development of advanced fault diagnosis technologies is becoming increasingly important. This paper presents an experimental setup for the acquisition of lithium-ion battery condition data. Different approaches for the early diagnosis and prediction of various LIBS faults are investigated. This will allows for investigation of the feasibility of using diverse types of gas sensors in large lithium-ion battery systems in addition to conventionally used battery monitoring tools.

articleTitle: Improved Adaptive Approach for Suppression of 1st and 3th Harmonic of Mains Interference in ECG Signals
abstract: This paper presents an improved adaptive method for first and third harmonic removal of mains interference from ECG signals. The method applies two notch filters removing the first and third harmonics of the interference, respectively. The adaptation of the first harmonic notch filter is performed by changing one of its coefficients according to the variations of the mains frequency. The corresponding coefficient in the third harmonic notch filter is recalculated on the base of the first harmonic notch filter's coefficient. The adapted two notch filters are pipelined on the ECG signal. Multiple experiments were performed on real ECG signals with sampling rates from 400 to 180000 Hz to which a synthesized mains interference was added. The experiments were performed in the MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of WSe2 Thin Flakes
abstract: The paper reports synthesis details of 2D WSe2 flakes, grown at short pre-deposition time of W layer/clusters subsequently followed by selenization using Thermally Assisted Conversion (TAC) method. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and Raman analysis reveal the formation of different flake shapes (mainly dendritic and triangular) with typical Raman modes for ultrathin films close to the monolayer limit.

articleTitle: Interference Wedged Structure for Remote and Purely Optical Intensity Control of a Powerful Laser Beam with a Low-Intensity Light
abstract: We develop our proposed devices, compact instruments for controlling powerful light by light, based on Interference Wedged Structures (IWS) that allow tuning for desired wavelength. The device (acting as optical transistor) exploits that the IWS's (CIWS's) gap with saturable absorber can be additionally illuminated by control light beam directly from the top open side of the IWS. The device can be used in scientific apparatus for laser pulse formation and in optical communication systems operating in high electromagnetic noise.

Author Keywords: purely optical control of light with light

articleTitle: Systems for Remote Access to FPGA Development Boards: Review
abstract: This report presents the study results of remote access systems for FPGA development hardware during the period 2008–2021. The possibilities and development of these systems are considered. The study made it possible to define the requirements and the expected final results in the implementation of a new system for remote access to FPGA development hardware, which is in the process of implementation in the “Automated design” laboratory at the KST department of the Technical University - Gabrovo.

articleTitle: Three-contact In-plane Sensitive Hall Devices
abstract: A new in-plane sensitive Hall configurations were suggested and tested. Each of them contains two identical rectangular n-type silicon slabs disposed in parallel. There are three elongated ohmic contacts on one of the surfaces of substrates. In one structure the contacts are asymmetrically arranged as output electrodes are outside the regions through which the currents flow. The other device is symmetrical, as contacts are at equal distances. Arrangements have low offset about 4mT, high sensitivity 36V/AT and operational volume <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$110 \times 100 \times 40 \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Role of Thermography in Cattle Smart Farming: A Review
abstract: Modern cattle smart farms are gradually adopting infrared thermography as an essential tool for evaluating the State-of-Health of their animals. The goal of our work is to introduce a more comprehensive animal model, aiding the next generation of intelligent bio-monitoring systems. Described are: bovine biology, tissue mechanics, hair covering effects, thermal windows for the biomedical observation and detection of different clinical conditions and infectious diseases. Discussed are the physiological and behavioral changes induced by animal handling and environmental influences.

articleTitle: Realizing a Cyber-Physical Systems Oriented Student Training for Ukrainian Students
abstract: In the framework of the Erasmus+ project “Development of practically-oriented student-centred education in the field of modelling of Cyber-Physical Systems”, in the first half of February 2022 a group of 12 Ukrainian engineering students (and 1 professor) participated in a two-week exchange program at KU Leuven Bruges Campus (Belgium). The mainly research-based training focused on a broad range of topics including renewable energy, sustainable material science and several applications of Cyber-Physical Systems.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Bipolar Programmable-Gain Amplifiers Using Digital Potentiometers
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical analysis and design procedure of versatile programmable amplifier circuits with bipolar gain. In particular, under analysis are two basic electronic circuits of single- and two-stage bipolar program-mable-gain amplifiers employing monolithic CMOS digital potentiometers. For both circuits, a single digital potentiometer is connected as a voltage divider in the negative feedback network of an op-amp. As a result of adjusting the position of the wiper of the potentiometer, the depth of the feedback changes, and hence the voltage gains change. Based on theoretical analysis of the circuits, analytical expressions for the basic static and dynamic parameters are derived. Moreover, using those formulas, approaches for selecting an appropriate circuit configuration and recommendations for selecting passive and active component values are proposed. The workability of the presented design recommendations is proved by computer simulations and experimental testing of sample analog circuits. The comparative analysis between simulation and measured results shows that the maximum relative error is up to 10%, which ensures a sufficient degree of accuracy in comparison to the tolerances of the electrical parameters.
